questions.problem: Find the average value of the function $f(x,y)=2x+y$ on the portion of the disk of radius $2$ centered at the origin, where $y\ge 0.$
questions.worked_solution:
First, let's sketch our region $D:$ 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14221067/assets/b5ba69ab02aa13e201b7b9113f6a36e705ad19e6412499504afc4f239459a8f3.png)

Notice that 

$$
\text{Area}(D)=\frac{1}{2}\cdot \pi \cdot {2}^{2}=2\pi .
$$

The average value of the function over a region $D$ is given by

$$
{f}_{\text{ave}}=\frac{1}{\text{Area}(D)}\,{∬}_{D}f(x,y)\,\text{d}A.
$$

We will use the change of variables formula in the form

$$
{∬}_{D}f(x,y)\text{ }dA={∬}_{Δ}\text{ }f(r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta )\,r\text{ }drd\theta .
$$

In polar coordinates $(r,\theta ),$ the region can be expressed as 

$$
Δ=\{(r,\theta )\,:\,0\le r\le 2,\,0\le \theta \le \pi \}.
$$

Using the change of variables formula, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}(2x+y)\,\text{d}A & ={∬}_{Δ}(2r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta +r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta )\,r\,\text{d}r\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }{\int }_{0}^{2}{r}^{2}(2\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta +\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta )\,\text{d}r\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }(2\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta +\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ){\int }_{0}^{2}{r}^{2}\,\text{d}r\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }(2\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta +\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta )\,{[\frac{{r}^{3}}{3}]}_{0}^{2}\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }(2\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta +\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta )(\frac{{2}^{3}}{3}-0)\text{d}\theta  \\  & =\frac{8}{3}{\int }_{0}^{\pi }(2\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta +\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta )\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =\frac{8}{3}[2\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta -\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ]_{0}^{\pi } \\  & =\frac{8}{3}((2\operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi )-\operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi ))-(2\operatorname{sin}⁡(0)-\operatorname{cos}⁡(0))) \\  & =\frac{8}{3}(1+1) \\  & =\frac{16}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, 

$$
{f}_{\text{ave}}=\frac{1}{2\pi }\cdot \frac{16}{3}=\frac{8}{3\pi }.
$$

questions.problem: Find the average value of the function $f(x,y)=y+{x}^{2}$ on the region $D=\{(x,y)\,:\,0\le x\le 2,\,x\le y\le 2x\}$ given that the area of the region is $2.$
questions.worked_solution:
Applying the average value formula, we find that the average value of the function is

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{\text{ave}} & =\frac{1}{\text{Area}(D)}\,{∬}_{D}f(x,y)\,\text{d}A \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{∬}_{D}y+{x}^{2}\,\text{d}A \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{x}^{2x}y+{x}^{2}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{0}^{2}[\frac{{y}^{2}}{2}+{x}^{2}y]_{y=x}^{y=2x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{0}^{2}[{x}^{3}+\frac{3{x}^{2}}{2}]\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{2}[\frac{{x}^{4}}{4}+\frac{{x}^{3}}{2}]_{x=0}^{x=2} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(8-0) \\  & =4.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: Find the average value of the function $f(x,y)=2x+3{y}^{2}$ on the region $D=\{(x,y)\,:\,0\le x\le 1,\,0\le y\le 2\}.$
questions.worked_solution:
First, notice that 

$$
\text{Area}(D)=1\cdot 2=2.
$$

Applying the average value formula, we find that the average value of the function is

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{\text{ave}} & =\frac{1}{\text{Area}(D)}\,{∬}_{D}f(x,y)\,\text{d}A \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{∬}_{D}(2x+3{y}^{2})\,\text{d}A \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{2}(2x+3{y}^{2})\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{0}^{1}[2xy+{y}^{3}]_{y=0}^{y=2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{0}^{1}(4x+8)\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{2}[2{x}^{2}+8x]_{x=0}^{x=1} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(2\cdot {1}^{2}+8\cdot 1) \\  & =\frac{10}{2} \\  & =5.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: Find the average value of the function $f(x,y)={y}^{2}$ on the disk of radius $2$ centered at the origin.
questions.worked_solution:
First, notice that 

$$
\text{Area}(D)=\pi \cdot {2}^{2}=4\pi .
$$

The average value of the function over a region $D$ is given by

$$
{f}_{\text{ave}}=\frac{1}{\text{Area}(D)}\,{∬}_{D}f(x,y)\,\text{d}A.
$$

We will use the change of variables formula in the form

$$
{∬}_{D}f(x,y)\text{ }dA={∬}_{Δ}\text{ }f(r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta )\,r\text{ }drd\theta .
$$

In polar coordinates $(r,\theta ),$ the region can be expressed as 

$$
Δ=\{(r,\theta )\,:\,0\le r\le 2,\,0\le \theta <2\pi \}.
$$

Using the change of variables formula, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}{y}^{2}\,\text{d}A & ={∬}_{Δ}(r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta )^{2}\,r\,\text{d}r\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2\pi }{\int }_{0}^{2}{r}^{3}{sin}^{2}⁡\theta \,\text{d}r\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2\pi }{sin}^{2}⁡\theta {\int }_{0}^{2}{r}^{3}\,\text{d}r\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2\pi }{sin}^{2}⁡\theta \,{[\frac{{r}^{4}}{4}]}_{0}^{2}\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2\pi }{sin}^{2}⁡\theta (4-0)\text{d}\theta  \\  & =4{\int }_{0}^{2\pi }{sin}^{2}⁡\theta \,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =4{\int }_{0}^{2\pi }\frac{1}{2}(1-\operatorname{cos}⁡2\theta )\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =2{[\theta -\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡2\theta ]}_{0}^{2\pi } \\  & =2[(2\pi -0)-\frac{1}{2}(\operatorname{sin}⁡4\pi -\operatorname{sin}⁡0)] \\  & =2\cdot 2\pi  \\  & =4\pi .\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, 

$$
{f}_{\text{ave}}=\frac{1}{4\pi }\cdot 4\pi =1.
$$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14221067/assets/f84a8fcd4ed668a6b94d5b084ade49dc8fc027feff4baea862e2feaf68221534.png)

Find the average value of the function $f(x,y)=y\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}$ on the semicircle shown above.
questions.worked_solution:
First, notice that 

$$
\text{Area}(D)=\frac{1}{2}\cdot \pi \cdot {1}^{2}=\frac{\pi }{2}.
$$

The average value of the function over a region $D$ is given by

$$
{f}_{\text{ave}}=\frac{1}{\text{Area}(D)}\,{∬}_{D}f(x,y)\,\text{d}A.
$$

We will use the change of variables formula in the form

$$
{∬}_{D}f(x,y)\text{ }dA={∬}_{Δ}\text{ }f(r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta )\,r\text{ }drd\theta .
$$

Notice that the region $D$ represents a portion of the disk of radius $1$ centered at 
$(-1,0).$

Cartesian and polar coordinates are connected by the following equations:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}x=r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  \\ y=r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \end{aligned}
$$

With that in mind, let's now write the $y=\sqrt{-{x}^{2}-2x}$ in polar coordinates:

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =\sqrt{-{x}^{2}-2x} \\ {y}^{2} & =-{x}^{2}-2x \\ {x}^{2}+{y}^{2} & =-2x \\ (r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta )^{2}+(r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta )^{2} & =-2r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  \\ {r}^{2}({cos}^{2}⁡\theta +{sin}^{2}⁡\theta ) & =-2r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  \\ {r}^{2} & =-2r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  \\ {r}^{2}+2r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  & =0 \\ r(r+2\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

 

Since $r$ cannot be identical to zero on the entire semicircle, we must have $r=-2\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta .$

Therefore, in polar coordinates $(r,\theta ),$ the region can be expressed as 

$$
Δ=\{(r,\theta )\,:\,0\le r\le -2\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,\frac{\pi }{2}\le \theta \le \pi \}.
$$

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}y\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}\,\text{d}A & ={∬}_{Δ}(r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta )\sqrt{(r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta )^{2}+(r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta )^{2}}\,r\,\text{d}r\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{\pi /2}^{\pi }\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta {\int }_{0}^{-2\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta }{r}^{3}\,\text{d}r\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{\pi /2}^{\pi }\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta [\frac{{r}^{4}}{4}]_{0}^{-2\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta }\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =\frac{1}{4}{\int }_{\pi /2}^{\pi }\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ((-2\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta )^{4}-{0}^{4})\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =\frac{1}{4}{\int }_{\pi /2}^{\pi }16\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta {cos}^{4}⁡\theta \,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =4{[-\frac{{cos}^{5}⁡\theta }{5}]}_{\pi /2}^{\pi } \\  & =-\frac{4}{5}({cos}^{5}⁡\pi -{cos}^{5}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2})) \\  & =\frac{4}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, 

$$
{f}_{\text{ave}}=\frac{1}{(\frac{\pi }{2})}\cdot \frac{4}{5}=\frac{8}{5\pi }.
$$
